items.title: 52986_Lawrence Brown oral history interview
items.q: So, Tizol and Tricky and I -- we roomed together.

ctx.x: Oh, definitely. And we were playing theaters at that time, and in the theaters, the trombones usually had a room together, and the saxes had a room together -- you know like that. So, Tizol and Tricky and I -- we roomed together. And Tizol was very anxious to get this

number on. And we used to try to figure out -- he couldn't remember exactly he'd like for the middle to go. And so, he'd make eight bars of extemporaneous playing in the middle and come back to the eight bars in the end. And -- but he wrote it.

items.title: 61531_Juan Tizol oral history interview
items.q: Lawrence Brown used to sit down at the end, and then I was next, then Tricky on the other side

ctx.x: Lawrence Brown used to sit down at the end, and then I was next, then Tricky on the other side; they used to come out and talk and want to find out this and that, and so forth. "What are you?" I'd say, "Sure, I'm white." "Well, what you doing playing with us?" Oh, well, I used to say the same thing I would tell everybody. "This is a big band the man has a good reputation, play for everybody -- kings, queens, everybody, the President and everybody." So ...

They used to go to Brown and ask him questions, too, and Brown would say, "Let's change the seat; you sit down here and I'll sit there." I'd say, "That's all right, it don't make no difference, I'll sit there." I knew what to answer.
